claim: Legacy Mode was tested end to end in headless Chrome
The test sequence was: setup → sign 11 → release and re-sign → lock in → full sim → result
There were no console errors during the headless Chrome test
Spin Draft still works as before after the changes
A new Game mode toggle exists at the top of the setup screen
The Game mode toggle offers two options: Spin Draft and Legacy Mode
In Legacy Mode, the Ratings row is hidden
In Legacy Mode, the Rating pool row is hidden
In Legacy Mode, prime ratings are always used
In Legacy Mode, Difficulty sets the budget instead of re-spins
Easy difficulty sets a budget of £600m in Legacy Mode
Medium difficulty sets a budget of £450m in Legacy Mode
Hard difficulty sets a budget of £330m in Legacy Mode
The 'How it works' steps change to match Legacy Mode when Legacy Mode is selected
Every player in the dataset appears once in the Legacy Mode draft screen
The dataset contains 2,287 players
Each player appears at their prime rating in the Legacy Mode draft screen
Each player appears with their club in the Legacy Mode draft screen
Each player appears with their season in the Legacy Mode draft screen
The Legacy Mode draft screen has a budget bar
The Legacy Mode draft screen has a search box
The search box ignores accents
The search box matches clubs
Searching 'ilkay' finds İlkay Gündoğan
The Legacy Mode draft screen has filters: Open slots, GK, DEF, MID, ATT, All
The player list is sorted by rating in Legacy Mode
Players the user can sign are shown first in the list
Players the user cannot sign are dimmed in the list
Players over budget are marked 'over budget'
Players that cannot be signed due to no open slot are marked 'no open spot'
The pricing formula is £5m × e^((rating − 75) / 7)
A rating of 80 costs approximately £10m
A rating of 85 costs approximately £21m
A rating of 90 costs approximately £43m
A rating of 94 costs approximately £75m
A rating of 99 costs approximately £154m
The £600m budget buys roughly an average-92 rated XI if money is spread evenly
The £450m budget buys roughly an average-90 rated XI if money is spread evenly
The £330m budget buys roughly an average-88 rated XI if money is spread evenly
A 90-rated side won the whole simulation about 42% of the time in testing
A 94-rated side went unbeaten about 22% of the time in testing
The game always keeps £1m back for each other empty slot so the user cannot get stuck
The user cannot spend their last pound while slots are still open
Tapping a player on the pitch allows the user to move or release them
Releasing a player refunds the full fee
Tapping an empty slot filters the list to that position line
A full XI is not locked automatically; the user must press 'Lock in XI →'
The teamsheet shows each player's fee
The teamsheet shows the total spend
The teamsheet has an 'Adjust XI' button to go back
All code changes are contained within index.html
The build() function now stores each prime entry's season's groups and positions
The existing fields in build() and their users are unchanged
The sim() function is untouched
The createRun() function is untouched
Formations logic is untouched
Slots logic is untouched
Legacy Mode picks go into the same filled array as Spin Draft
Legacy Mode picks go through the same runSim() function as Spin Draft
The overall calculation now happens before the draft screens
The overall calculation is moved earlier so the Legacy pitch can show OVR
The overall calculation itself is unchanged
New CSS classes are prefixed .fd-lg-*
Buying Ronaldo, Messi and Lewandowski first left £26m for eight players
Buying Ronaldo, Messi and Lewandowski first resulted in a 79-rated side
Budgets are stored as single constants under DIFF[*].budget
The price curve is stored as a single constant called legacyPrice
The saved best run (fd_best) is shared between Spin Draft and Legacy Mode
A Legacy Mode run can replace the Spin Draft best run in fd_best
